angle: WR/TE break mechanics from Combine route drills (Break G) matched to the same NFL route families (slant/out/hitch/in/corner), tested against season separation over expected on held-out draft classes; bounded null plus a held-out draft-price finding
metric_name: Break G: mean acceleration magnitude (g) over the 1.0 s centred on the sharpest point of the first route break, z-scored within drill x Combine year, averaged over route drills and reliability-shrunk; identical code on NFL snaps; rule frozen and hashed in frozen_rule.json
headline_number: Held-out slope -1.2 in of season SOE per sd of Break G (90% interval -3.5 to +1.0, n=116, shuffle p=0.38); every variant's upper end <= +1.9 in, below the pre-set +3 in margin. Clubs draft +1 sd Break G receivers 14% earlier on held-out classes [4, 24], all three classes, leave-one-player-out 12-15%
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round_11/revised (8.29). Data science: (1) QB adjustment. The passer is parsed from every sampled play description (97 QBs, 4,071 snaps). The QB effect is estimated leave-player-out and empirical-Bayes shrunk, then subtracted from season SOE. Held-out slope -1.1 [-3.7, +1.0]; QB environment sd is only 0.8 in. (2) Weak forecast addressed three ways: ridge baseline with leave-one-class-out penalty (calibration 0.52/3.95/1.86, over-shrinks; slope -0.7 [-2.7, +1.5]); forecast entered as a covariate so its calibration slope is estimated (-0.6 [-2.3, +1.9]); leave-one-player-out range -1.7 to -0.5 (Nacua most influential) and jackknife interval -3.5 to +1.1. (3) Price and targets-per-route claims get held-out class tests. Price: 14% earlier [4, 24], p=0.02, all three classes, LOPO 12-15%. Targets/route: +2.0 pts [0.0, 4.2] held out, but 0.8 and p=0.25 without Nacua, so it sits in Limitations. (4) A ledger table of all 41 tests sits next to the headline. Football: the lede defines SOE in plain words; a plain GM scatter (Fig 1) with the six card players labelled opens the piece; the so-what is three actions (leave it out of the grade, don't pay, run reps twice) plus a positive use (the discount on soft drill cutters with good tape). Decision card: Action + Cost only, per-player scheme-specific re-watch prompts (man/zone, slot/wide, best/worst route with snap counts), and a single scout verdict, 'draft on tape, ignore the drill cut'. Writeup: physics paragraph cut to one sentence; timing bullet, Timing appendix, 18-definition table and Boutte false-positive paragraph dropped; protocol cut to three sentences; jargon moved to the appendix. 1,744 words (from 1,836 by check.py). Viz: the six-player card is now Fig 2, placed right after the metric, with overlaid drill vs NFL cut paths in one rotated frame, the Break G window marked, and shared-axis dot-and-interval strips for Break G and SOE vs forecast. Fig 3 panel 2 gets a shuffle-null band; panel 3 is a per-player caterpillar with the pooled slope +1.5 [-2.0, +5.0]. Fig 4 is one labelled strip with n on each row, per-class dots on one row, LOPO and 18-definition ranges, a catches axis directly under the inches axis, and 'pre-set margin' wording. Old Fig 1 (one-cut physics) removed. 4 figures + 2 tables.
open_risks: Headline is still a bounded null; losses down to -3.5 in are not excluded
Not a blind test: all three classes were seen before the rule was frozen; 2026 is the first true out-of-sample score
The freely fitted QB coefficient has the wrong sign (-2.02), so the adjustment subtracts the QB environment at face value. The QB effects come from sampled snaps, half selected for high EPA
Ridge does not fix forecast calibration (2024 slope 3.95). Only the forecast-as-covariate version estimates calibration directly, and it moves the point estimate to -0.6
Decision-card scheme splits rest on 5 to 31 sampled snaps per cell, so they are re-watch prompts, not grades
The price finding is an association (scouts may value route detail seen in the same drill); the 'discount' positive use is not tested as a payoff beyond pick (0.1 in [-1.3, +1.6])
